name: Vertex-Free Two-Unit Profiles Are Separated by Their Passive Carriers
statement: For a two-unit holonomy wing with $|K|\le9$ and $\eta=0$, the profile with shores of orders two and three meeting in one concept is impossible. In each remaining profile—disjoint shores of orders two and four, disjoint three-concept shores, or disjoint two-concept cycle shores with a third disjoint singleton shore—the two cycle shores supply two disjoint acquired direction pairs. Hence every feasible two-unit wing is pair-rich.
proof: Exact counting gives $|L|=1$, $|K|=9$, and a complete description by collars and punctured fibres. In the intersecting $2$--$3$ profile, the two anchors of the edges in one passive direction differ in that passive direction and in an active direction, so they are nonadjacent, contradicting connectedness of the ample edge carrier. In each remaining profile, every cycle shore is disjoint from all other nonempty shores and contains an active edge. Below, its collar is the only edge in the passive direction, so the associated active--passive pair is not shattered; above, the shore edge and its flip form the full square. Applying this to both cycle shores gives acquired pairs, and the direction-separation lemma makes them disjoint.
